[19] assistant: You’re mixing up `pnpm audit --fix` with “update all packages.”

For this repo, `pnpm audit --fix` does **not** generally upgrade everything in `dependencies` / `devDependencies`. In pnpm 9, its help says:

> `--fix`: Add overrides to the package.json file in order to force non-vulnerable versions of the dependencies

So the correction is:

- `pnpm audit` reports known vulnerable packages.
- `pnpm audit --fix` tries to resolve vulnerable transitive versions by adding `pnpm.overrides` to `package.json`.
- It is not the same as `pnpm update`, and it will not necessarily bump your direct dependencies like `next`, `react`, `typescript`, etc.
- If the vulnerable package is a direct dependency, or the fix requires a semver-major upgrade, `audit --fix` may not do what you expect.
- If no safe override exists, or the advisory requires changing a top-level package range, you still need to update manually.

The usual flow is:

```powershell
pnpm audit
pnpm update
pnpm audit --fix
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm lint
```

For targeted upgrades:

```powershell
pnpm update next eslint-config-next
pnpm update --latest some-package
```

So: you weren’t wrong that it can fix some audit findings, but you were off in expecting it to “update all packages.” In pnpm, audit fix is mostly an overrides-based vulnerability mitigation tool, not a general dependency upgrade command.

import { getEnv, getRequiredEnv } from "../lib/env";

export type DbDialect = "sqlite" | "pg";

export function isNextBuildPhase() {
  return getEnv("NEXT_PHASE") === "phase-production-build";
}

function normalizeDbDialect(value: string | undefined): DbDialect | undefined {
  if (!value) return undefined;
  const v = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (v === "pg" || v === "postgres" || v === "postgresql") return "pg";
  if (v === "sqlite" || v === "sqlite3") return "sqlite";
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Runtime DB selection.
 *
 * Precedence:
 * - During `next build`, force SQLite in-memory to keep builds green.
 * - If `PG_DATABASE_URL` is set at runtime, use Postgres.
 * - Otherwise use SQLite (via `DATABASE_URL` or the default file).
 */
export function getDbDialect(): DbDialect {
  if (isNextBuildPhase()) return "sqlite";

  // Explicit override when both URLs are present (or to force one backend).
  const forced = normalizeDbDialect(getEnv("DB_DIALECT"));
  if (forced) return forced;

  // Default precedence: prefer Postgres when configured.
  if (getEnv("PG_DATABASE_URL")) return "pg";
  return "sqlite";
}

export function getSqliteDatabaseUrl(): string {
  return getEnv("DATABASE_URL") ?? "file:./data/lego.sqlite";
}

export function getPgDatabaseUrl(): string {
  return getRequiredEnv("PG_DATABASE_URL");
}
